did_you_know.text: Did you know? Construction of the Temple began in the fourth year of Solomon’s reign, in the month of Ziv—the second month—480 years after the Israelites left Egypt.
Did you know? The Temple’s main dimensions were 60 cubits long, 20 cubits wide, and 30 cubits high.
Did you know? Side chambers were built around the walls of the main hall and the inner sanctuary. They were arranged in three levels, with widths increasing from five to six to seven cubits.
Did you know? The stones for the Temple were prepared in advance, so no sound of hammers, axes, or any other iron tool was heard at the Temple site during its construction.
Did you know? The different levels of the side chambers were reached by spiral staircases, described as “lulim.”

Did you know? The word of the Lord to Solomon emphasizes that building the Temple alone was not enough: fulfilling the promise depended on walking in the Lord’s ways, carrying out His judgments, and keeping His commandments.

Did you know? Inside the Temple, the inner sanctuary—the Most Holy Place—was set apart. Its length, width, and height were each 20 cubits, and in front of it was the main hall, which was 40 cubits long.
Did you know? Two cherubim made of olive wood were placed in the inner sanctuary. Each was 10 cubits high, and their outstretched wings touched one another and the walls.
Did you know? The walls of the Temple were decorated with carvings of cherubim, palm trees, and flowers, and the Temple was overlaid with gold inside and out.
Did you know? The Temple was completed in the eleventh year of Solomon’s reign, in the month of Bul—the eighth month—and its construction took seven years in all.
